key_insight: UltraQuant shows that 4-bit KV caching can preserve agent quality while substantially improving latency and throughput in long-context, multi-turn serving workloads.
engineering_relevance: The paper targets a practical bottleneck in agent serving by combining cache compression with GPU-kernel and data-format optimizations to keep utilization high under concurrency.
method: Benchmarked 4-bit KV caching for multi-round agent workloads.
Used TurboQuant-style rotation, codebook quantization, asymmetric K/V handling, and block-scale variants.
Added AMD GPU serving optimizations and an UltraQuant FP4 path with FP8 queries, FP4 KV tensors, and UE8M0 group scales.
evidence_signal: On a long-context, multi-turn agentic workload, UltraQuant improved P50 time-to-first-token by 3.47x in late cache-pressured rounds (2.3x overall) and increased output throughput by 1.63x versus FP8 KV caching.
watch_item: The approach depends on specialized quantization choices and AMD CDNA4-specific support, so portability and stability across other models or GPU stacks may require extra validation.
paper_title: UltraQuant: 4-bit KV Caching for Context-Heavy Agents
